subject: Dedicated deployment — data zoning & wipe criteria review
messages:
From: Claire R. / ClearPath Finance <security@clearpathfinance.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.example.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarification: dedicated deployment data zoning and deletion criteria

Hi David,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are reviewing the Dedicated deployment contract language and need a concise explanation of how Redwood guarantees data zoning and the operational steps for tenant-scoped deletion. Specifically: 

- Where are customer data shards and snapshots physically stored when a tenant is pinned to a US region?
- What is the timeline and trigger set for a tenant purge request (both soft-delete and hard-delete)?
- Can you provide a sample wipe playbook and evidence artifacts (logs, snapshot deletion events) that we can attach to our audit?

Our auditors want a short matrix (policy → operational artifact) and an example timeline for a standard tenant deletion request (no legal hold). Can you send those or schedule a quick call?

Claire
Security Operations
ClearPath Finance

--
Note: We may bring our auditors (acme-cloud-audits) to the call if helpful.
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.example.com>
To: Claire R. / ClearPath Finance <security@clearpathfinance.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarification: dedicated deployment data zoning and deletion criteria

Hi Claire — thanks for the clear asks. Putting the high-level answers here and attaching a draft matrix for your auditors.

Short answers (summary):
- Physical storage: For Dedicated region-pinned tenants we provision tenant slices on GPU nodes within the requested cloud region (control plane in Redwood-managed region). Persistent snapshots are stored on region-local block storage and object storage (single-region replication by default for Dedicated unless customer requests cross-region replica).
- Purge timeline: Typical workflow — request received → soft-delete + snapshot freeze (t+0) → retention grace window (configurable, default 7 days) → hard-delete job queued (t+7) → snapshot and block object zeroization + metadata tombstone (t+7 to t+10) → final verification & log export (t+10). We can accelerate to meet tighter SLAs; need procurement sign-off for expedited wipe.
- Artifacts: We can provide playbook PDF (wipe-playbook-v1.pdf), a matrix mapping policy items to audit artifacts, and redacted example logs showing snapshot deletion events. The attached spreadsheet includes the mapping you asked for.

Proposed next steps:
1) Review the attached data-zoning-matrix.xlsx and confirm any missing evidence columns.
2) If acceptable, we can run a dry-run purge in a dedicated sandbox tenant and capture the evidence you want (takes ~48–72 hours to complete the run and package artifacts).
3) Schedule a 30-min alignment call with your auditors and our ops engineering (Laura + Ben).

If you want the accelerated (t+2) hard-delete timeline we will need an SLA addendum; I can route that to Sales but Laura/Ben can advise on operational feasibility.

Attachments: data-zoning-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), wipe-playbook-v1.pdf (playbook)

—
David Kim
Head of Trust & Safety, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.example.com>, Claire R. / ClearPath Finance <security@clearpathfinance.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarification: dedicated deployment data zoning and deletion criteria

Thanks — read the matrix and left a few operational notes inline. Key clarifications: 

- Snapshots: We do not cross-region replicate snapshot binaries for a standard Dedicated pin. Any cross-region replica is configuration-driven and documented in the SOW.
- Block zeroization: We overwrite metadata and issue object deletion with cloud provider lifecycle APIs; in some cases underlying physical disk reallocation by the provider can delay physical zeroing — we provide the deletion events and provider confirmation as evidence.
- Legal hold path: If customer requests hold, we suspend the hard-delete queue and record hold metadata; auditors will receive a separate hold clearance artifact.

Ben, please confirm expected artifacts list for the dry-run: I documented snapshot deletion event (timestamped), object-delete events (provider request IDs), and our internal purge job runbook excerpt.

Laura
Sr. Director, Customer Security Operations
